You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

Based on the chest X-ray findings, which of the following best describes the characteristics of the pulmonary nodule identified in Figure 1, and what is the most likely diagnosis? Consider the nodule's definition, location, and potential etiology based on the radiographic evidence and the clinical history provided.

A) A well-defined, homogeneous nodule in the right upper lobe, likely a benign sclerosing haemangioma.
B) A poorly defined, heterogeneous nodule in the right upper lobe, likely an inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour.
C) A well-defined, heterogeneous nodule in the right lower lobe, likely a malignant neoplasm.
D) A poorly defined, homogeneous nodule in the left upper lobe, likely a hamartoma.
E) A well-defined, homogeneous nodule in the left upper lobe, likely a nodular lymphoid hyperplasia.
F) A poorly defined, heterogeneous nodule in the right upper lobe, likely a malignant neoplasm.
